title: Building a Corpus from Files and APIs
text: data already tabular – manual tracker, institutional export, spreadsheet works – robust entry point sm_corpus_from_tables(). validates required columns, coerces types, fills missing optional tables correctly-typed 0-row tibbles, returns ready sm_corpus, side-stepping format-specific parsers entirely. works-corpus perfectly valid: can pass works, authorships, sources, institutions, references, concepts, etc. named list elements.
code: works <- data.frame(   work_id = paste0("W", 1:3),   title = c("Spatial transcriptomics in cancer",             "Immune checkpoint resistance",             "A biomarker discovery cohort"),   year = c("2019", "2020", "2021"),   # character -> coerced to integer   doi = paste0("10.1234/example.", 1:3),   cited_by_count = c(12, 5, 1) ) corpus <- sm_corpus_from_tables(list(works = works)) #> ℹ works: coerced column year and cited_by_count to the schema type. #> ℹ works: filled missing column abstract, type, source_id, oa_status, language, #>   pmid, arxiv_id, openalex_id, is_retracted, retraction_date, and #>   last_refreshed with typed `NA`. corpus #>  #> ── <sm_corpus> ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Works: 3 | Authors: 0 | Institutions: 0 #> Years: 2019 - 2021 #> Sources (journals): 0 #> Embeddings: none #> Status: Unlocked (last refreshed: never)

title: Building a Corpus from Files and APIs
text: corpus, fold cached enrichment (metrics table, citation cache, …) sm_materialise() rather hand-writing join. matches key, fills NA cells (replaces overwrite = TRUE), returns schema-valid corpus — avoiding classic bind_rows() bug NULL element silently becomes logical column.
code: metrics <- data.frame(work_id = corpus$works$work_id,                       cnci = c(1.4, 0.8, 1.1)) corpus <- sm_materialise(corpus, sources = list(works = metrics)) #> ✔ Materialised 3 enrichment rows into works (+1 column). "cnci" %in% names(corpus$works) #> [1] TRUE

title: Modern Citation Indicators
text: sm_self_citation() derives author (institution) self-citation reference lists already corpus — per-citation API calls. returns per-entity per-work tibbles plus provenance trail showing works drove self-citation, suitable institutional report. h/g/m indices accept self_corrected = TRUE, recomputes index removing self-citations (always <= uncorrected value):
code: sc_corpus <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "example_self_citation_corpus.rds",                                  package = "scimapR")) sc <- sm_self_citation(sc_corpus, level = "author") sc$by_entity #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   entity_id n_citations_received n_self_citations self_citation_share #>   <chr>                    <int>            <int>               <dbl> #> 1 A1                           5                4                 0.8 #> 2 A2                           4                2                 0.5 head(sc$provenance) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>   citing_work_id cited_work_id shared_author_id #>   <chr>          <chr>         <chr>            #> 1 W2             W1            A1               #> 2 W4             W2            A1               #> 3 W4             W2            A2               #> 4 W5             W3            A2               #> 5 W6             W2            A1               #> 6 W6             W4            A1 merge(   sm_metric_h_index(sc_corpus, "author"),   sm_metric_h_index(sc_corpus, "author", self_corrected = TRUE),   by = "author_id", suffixes = c("", "_corrected") ) #>   author_id h_index h_index_corrected #> 1        A1       3                 3 #> 2        A2       3                 3 #> 3        A3       1                 1

text: comprehensive toolkit bibliometric scientometric analysis, designed complement foundational 'bibliometrix' package (Aria & Cuccurullo, 2017, doi:10.1016/j.joi.2017.08.007 ). Provides unified ingestion major bibliographic sources including 'OpenAlex', 'Crossref', 'Semantic Scholar', 'PubMed', 'arXiv', 'bioRxiv', 'ORCID', 'Overton', 'Unpaywall', 'Scopus', 'Web Science' exports; classical science mapping (co-citation, bibliographic coupling, co-authorship, co-word networks); modern citation indicators (CD index, Relative Citation Ratio, field-normalized scores, Uzzi novelty); embedding-based research cluster discovery; structured research-question objects optional LLM-grounded screening; author trajectory analysis; equity representation auditing explicit confidence method reporting; reproducible--construction corpus certificates enabling exact re-derivation corpus; retrieval-grounded conversational corpus exploration; comprehensive 'shiny' application publication-ready figure table export. Output fully 'tidyverse'-compatible tibble-based corpora, 'viridis'-themed 'ggplot2' visualizations, 'tidygraph' network objects.

Umlauts, accented letters sharp s word characters: \w consumes , \b finds edge word starts ends one, POSIX classes [[:alpha:]] Unicode-aware . title: Gender representation audit — sm_audit_gender
text: Known limitations automated gender inference: Name-based methods assign binary gender proxy, capture full spectrum gender identity. Accuracy varies dramatically cultural context: names East Asian, South Asian, many African cultures poorly served Western-trained models. Non-binary, transgender, gender-diverse individuals systematically misclassified. method account name changes, pen names, initialised first names.

This does not #> capture the full spectrum of gender identity. #> • Name-based methods have variable accuracy across cultures. East Asian, South #> Asian, and many African names are poorly served by Western-trained models. #> • Non-binary, transgender, and gender-diverse individuals are systematically #> misclassified by these methods. #> • Initialised first names (e.g., 'J. Smith') cannot be classified and reduce #> coverage. #> • These results should be reported with confidence intervals and #> method-specific caveats in any publication. #> • We recommend against using these results to make claims about individual #> researchers' gender identity.

what: Build an author trajectory analysis — sm_author_trajectory
title: Build an author trajectory analysis — sm_author_trajectory
text: Analyses career trajectory single author within corpus, partitioning publication record n_periods career stages. period, function computes: Career stages: dominant topics (three concept names found period's works) publication volume. Topic pivots: much research focus shifted periods, measured Jaccard distance concept sets. Collaborator turnover: Jaccard similarity co-author sets across consecutive periods, plus counts new, kept, lost collaborators. Emerging collaborators: co-authors first appear recent period. H-index curve: cumulative h-index end period. Novelty curve: average concept novelty per period, mean number distinct concept names per work (works concepts). Citation acceleration: mean citations per period relative corpus-wide mean years.

text: tibble columns work_id cd_index. CD index ranges -1 (consolidating) +1 (disruptive). Works without sufficient citation data receive NA.

title: Calculate the CD (disruption) index — sm_metric_disruption
text: CD index defined : $$CD = \frac{n_i - n_j}{n_i + n_j + n_k}$$ focal work f: n_i Number works cite f cite f's references (disruptive citations). n_j Number works cite f least one f's references (consolidating citations). n_k Number works cite least one f's references cite f (ignored--referencing citations). CD index near +1 indicates focal work highly disruptive: citers tend ignore references. CD index near -1 indicates focal work consolidates existing ideas. citations works inside corpus count. Items keyed cited_work_id, else normalised DOI, else OpenAlex id, else upper-case reference text whitespace squished final periods removed. Identifier kinds kept separate. linked_only = TRUE restores earlier behaviour warns none points corpus works. Empty input (zero works, zero references, pairs threshold) returns empty undirected tbl_graph.

title: Build a co-word (co-occurrence) network — sm_network_coword
text: Constructs undirected co-word network. Nodes represent terms edge connects two terms co-occur within work. Edge weight equals number works terms appear.

title: Build a co-word (co-occurrence) network — sm_network_coword
code: sm_network_coword(   corpus,   field = c("concepts", "title", "abstract", "keywords"),   ngram = 1L,   min_freq = 5L,   stopwords = NULL,   vocabulary = NULL,   call = rlang::caller_env() )

title: Build a co-word (co-occurrence) network — sm_network_coword
text: corpus sm_corpus object. field Character; text field extract terms . One "concepts" (default, uses corpus$concepts), "title", "abstract", "keywords". ngram Integer; free-text fields ("title", "abstract"), n-gram size tokenise . Defaults 1L (unigrams). min_freq Integer; minimum document frequency term must included. Defaults 5L. stopwords Character vector additional stopwords remove tokenising free text. Combined tidytext::stop_words. Set NULL (default) additional stopwords. vocabulary field = "keywords" "concepts", concept vocabularies take terms : names vocabularies families sm_concept_vocabularies(), "author-keywords" "indexer_keyword". NULL (default) means author keywords "keywords" (see Details) every vocabulary "concepts". Must NULL "title" "abstract", whose terms come text. call Caller environment error reporting.

title: Build a co-word (co-occurrence) network — sm_network_coword
text: tidygraph::tbl_graph object (undirected). Nodes carry name (term) freq (document frequency). Edges carry weight column (co-occurrence count).

title: Build a co-word (co-occurrence) network — sm_network_coword
text: field = "concepts", terms come concept_name column corpus$concepts (tokenisation needed), every vocabulary named vocabulary. field = "keywords", terms whole keywords corpus$concepts, tokenised. default author keywords (author_keyword family: author-keywords, manual-tags); corpus without falls back indexer keywords (indexer_keyword family: Keywords Plus, Scopus index keywords, Zotero automatic tags MeSH) message, corpus neither gives empty network message. fallback applies whole corpus, per work. field "title" "abstract", text tokenised tidytext::unnest_tokens() using chosen ngram size stopwords removed. Terms lower-cased, terms min_freq dropped. Empty input returns empty undirected tbl_graph.

text: tidygraph::tbl_graph object (undirected). Nodes carry name (work ID) columns corpus$works. Edges carry weight column (cosine similarity, 0 1).

title: Build a semantic similarity network — sm_network_semantic
text: Work IDs embedding row names must unique. Repeated IDs stop class scimapR_duplicate_ids; use sm_validate() inspect . Embeddings must present corpus$embeddings (numeric matrix row names matching work_id). Use sm_embed_works() compute . title: Read BibTeX files — sm_read_bib
text: native parser follows BibTeX format specification described original BibTeX documentation (Patashnik, 1988). Field values may enclosed braces double-quotes may span multiple lines. String concatenation # supported; @string @preamble entries skipped. Protective braces removed titles, journals, abstracts, keywords DOIs; escaped braces remain literal. Common LaTeX accent commands (\", \', \^, \~, \=, \., \c, \v, \u, \H, \k, \r, backslash followed grave accent) decode precomposed letters available, else bare letter. Letter commands \ss, \o, \O, \aa, \AA, \ae, \AE, \oe, \OE, \l, \L \also decode, \&, \%, \$, \# \_. DOI cleaning removes braces decodes five escapes. Ties (~), -- math expressions remain written. Whitespace outside math collapsed trimmed. lowercase outside braces separates authors; comma outside braces flips name surname-first given-name-first. Braced corporate names stay together, trailing others retained. Quoted field values end quote outside braces. first isolated four-digit year (1000–2999) year used, falling back BibLaTeX date field year present.

Files without PT record still return empty corpus. record begins PT  (publication type) ends ER. Field tags two uppercase letters followed single space. Continuation lines begin three spaces. Tags parsed: AU AF (authors), TI (title), (source), SN EI (ISSN electronic ISSN), J9 JI (source abbreviations), AB (abstract), DI (DOI), PY (year), DT (document type), LA (language), TC (times cited), UT (accession number, kept provenance), PM (PubMed ID), C1 (addresses), RP (corresponding authors), CR (cited references), DE (author keywords), ID (Keywords Plus), WC (Web Science categories) SC (research areas). tags read. distinct becomes row sources, issn_l SN (EI SN missing), issn holding SN EI, abbreviations J9 JI columns abbreviation iso_abbreviation. DE, ID, WC SC become concepts, one row per ;-separated term, vocabularies "author-keywords", "keywords-plus", "wos-category" "wos-subject-category" sm_concept_vocabularies(). Terms keep case file. Author names stored AU form, "J Smith" "Smith, J", authors$display_name_alternatives keeps name file writes , tells surname several words "Garcia Lopez" initials. parsers write one authorship row per author address. names brackets C1 link authors addresses: name belongs author full name (AF), else one surname initials, else one surname first initial, short surname "" never takes address "Chen". address C1 lists without names, older records , belongs every author record, gets row . address whose names designate none authors belongs author single-author record else nobody. corresponding authors come RP, names "(corresponding author)" ("(reprint author)" older files), case, name address line one line. authors names designate, matched like names C1, get is_corresponding = TRUE rows authors FALSE. name fits several authors equally (namesakes surname initials), one whose C1 addresses include address RP gives name meant; tell apart, get NA. record without RP, whose RP designates none authors certain, gets NA (unknown) authors; native parser reports number records verbose = TRUE. title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: Stability contracts, enrichment materializer, self-citation-corrected metrics, plus verify--harden pass three v0.3.0 fixes recurred heavy use. new behaviour opt-; breaking changes.

title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: New ?scimapR-stability topic documents package’s accessor return-type contract: documented accessor’s column set changes via lifecycle deprecation NEWS.md entry. audited accessors stable shapes listed . sm_coverage_breakdowns() gains tidy = TRUE (default): guaranteed long tibble (dimension, level, n_reference, n_matched, recall, n_corpus, precision, f1). tidy = FALSE returns legacy recall-shape. (silent list -> tibble change 0.2.0 0.3.0 motivated contract.)

title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: Exported sm_affiliation_signals(), sm_affiliation_methods(), sm_match_types() (describe = TRUE level + description). match_signal, match_method, coverage match_type columns now factors exact levels, downstream filtering drift.

title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: reported real corpus; now regression test reproducing recurrence. C1 sm_its(outcome = "cnci"): resolver now also searches documented impact side columns works (fnci, rcr, ncs, mncs, field_citation_ratio) corpus$metrics table, addition works$cnci works$cited_by_count. impact anywhere errors naming every column inspected. (v0.3 checked works$cnci / cited_by_count, impact side column still produced “0 observations”.) C2 sm_count(level = "institution"): structured IDs absent now clusters raw_affiliation via sm_affiliation_match() (canonical names matched, raw string otherwise) warning, instead counting raw strings verbatim. Absent raw affiliation -> 0-row tibble + warning. C3 network plot precompute = TRUE confirmed; max_nodes cap now opt-(NULL default) large renders unchanged unless cap requested. ~2,000-node graph builds precompute = TRUE re-prints without recomputing layout.

title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: sm_materialise(corpus, sources, .= NULL, overwrite = FALSE) joins cached enrichment (named list tibbles / RDS / parquet paths, cache dir) matching sub-tibbles key, returning validated sm_corpus. Missing keys warn (error); overlapping columns fill NA unless overwrite = TRUE. Added internal type-safe row-bind helper (.sm_bind_rows) returns typed template instead logical-column degenerate parts NULL/empty; audited package’s existing bind_rows() sites (found safe, guarded behind length checks typed tibbles).

title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: sm_self_citation(corpus, level = c("author", "institution")) computes self-citation corpus reference network (quota-light reference overlap; per-citation API calls), returning by_entity, by_work, provenance tibble (citing_work_id, cited_work_id, shared_author_id/shared_institution_id) (F1). Empty references -> warning + typed empty result (spin). sm_metric_h_index(), sm_metric_g_index(), sm_metric_m_index() gain self_corrected = FALSE; TRUE index recomputed removing self-citations (author/institution levels). corrected index always <= uncorrected one.

title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: sm_affiliation_summary() now includes example_evidence (representative matched-evidence string per institution x signal) alongside factorised match_signal, reader can see signal matched evidence.

title: scimapR 0.4.0
text: inst/extdata/example_self_citation_corpus.rds: small references-bearing synthetic corpus self-citation examples/tests.

title: scimapR 0.3.0
text: Real-use refinements running v0.2.0 ~6,853-work corpus: robustness fixes, friendlier API shapes, two new capabilities, vignettes ship installed binary. public API preserved (deprecation paths ).

title: scimapR 0.3.0
text: A1 sm_its(outcome = "cnci") longer fails cryptic “yearly observations: 0” impact lives outside cited_by_count. resolver now searches, order, works$cnci, corpus$metrics table, works$cited_by_count (deriving FNCI); none populated raises informative error naming columns inspected. A2 sm_count(level = "institution") falls back authorships$raw_affiliation (cli warning results un-disambiguated) structured institution IDs absent, warns rather returning silent empty result institution data exists. A3 sm_metric_disruption() sm_metric_novelty() fast-exit warning reference network empty/absent instead spinning; disruption index rewritten O(1) adjacency lookups (longer O(n^2)) now shows cli progress bar. sm_audit_summary() shows progress bar across sub-audits. A4 Network plots (sm_plot_citation_network(), sm_plot_collab()) gain precompute = TRUE (eager layout -> self-contained plain ggplot prints cheaply knitr/callr/workflowr subprocesses) max_nodes cap (default 200) large graphs.

title: scimapR 0.3.0
text: B1 sm_coverage_audit()$breakdowns now single flat tibble (dimension, level, n_reference, n_matched, recall). previous nested list remains available $breakdowns_nested one release. New accessor sm_coverage_breakdowns() returns/filters flat tibble. B2 sm_affiliation_match() documents added columns gains sm_affiliation_summary() — tidy works/authorships breakdown institution match signal, also surfaced cli summary completion. B3 sm_corpus_from_tables() promoted ingestion vignette recommended “bring relational data” entry point.

title: scimapR 0.3.0
text: C1 sm_coverage_audit(..., index_table = ) additionally assesses journal indexability (reusing sm_journal_in_index()), adding issn/indexable columns $matches $indexability summary. Output unchanged index_table NULL. C2 sm_affiliation_match() returns match_signal (name_token/email_domain/postcode) match_evidence (matched substring/domain/code) audit trail, plus opt-postcode_signal = TRUE matcher (default existing matches stable).

title: scimapR 0.3.0
text: D1 Vignettes now ship installed binary; browse offline vignette(package = "scimapR") / browseVignettes("scimapR"), online pkgdown site. New inst/extdata/ fixtures: example_affiliation_postcode.csv.

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: new capability layer research-coverage, affiliation-attribution, policy-evaluation analyses, plus four reproducible bug fixes. existing functionality, sm_corpus schema, bibliometrix interop, Shiny app preserved.

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: sm_coverage_audit() computes recall, precision, F1 corpus ground-truth reference (manual tracker, ORCID set, repository export, another sm_corpus), per-year/source/affiliation breakdowns full match provenance. Returns sm_coverage object print, summary, autoplot methods. sm_journal_in_index() verifies source coverage user-supplied journal master list normalised ISSN (print electronic), fully offline. sm_reconcile() performs content-based symmetric diff (DOI fuzzy title) returning sm_reconciliation (in_both/only_a/only_b + provenance), print/summary/autoplot. sm_diff_corpora() now marked superseded favour (continues work unchanged).

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: sm_affiliation_match() tags authorships institutions using multilingual / synonym-aware dictionary email-domain fallback, handling multiple affiliations per author. sm_attribute_institution() rolls matches controlled vocabulary (ROR-backed via offline ROR table, custom vocabulary). sm_affiliation_dict: default, documented, user-overridable dictionary.

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: sm_its(): turnkey interrupted time series (level + slope terms, counterfactual, autoplot), automatic exclusion citation-immature years citation-based outcomes. sm_did(): difference--differences treated vs control institution sets. sm_synth(): synthetic-control helper (optional tidysynth, graceful error absent).

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: sm_citation_maturity() flags citation-immature recent years (citation_mature / cnci_provisional), wired sm_its(). sm_count(): full vs fractional counting institution / author / source level (output credit fractionally-weighted impact).

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: sm_metric_summary(robust = TRUE) reports medians bootstrap CIs %PP(top-10%) alongside means (base-R resampling default; boot optional; reproducible via seed).

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: sm_figure_manifest() scans figure directory captions / alt-text / dimensions manifest (optional magick/png, sidecar caption files, CSV/YAML output). sm_corpus_from_tables(): documented, validating constructor relational set data frames — recommended ingestion path arbitrary tabular sources.

title: scimapR 0.2.0
text: G1 sm_fetch_openalex(engine = "native"): abstract reconstruction OpenAlex inverted index now type-stable never aborts fetch empty/NULL/malformed record (longer passes invalid .default purrr::map_chr()). G2 sm_fetch_openalex(engine = "openalexR"): long DOI (ID) lists auto-batched API’s -filter limit via new batch_size argument, row-bound de-duplicated. G3 sm_read_bib(engine = "bibliometrix"): field-sparse @article longer triggers “undefined columns selected”; scimapR wrapper catches failure falls back native parser (clean-room rule preserved). G4 native BibTeX engine performance: parser rewritten per-character substr()/grepl() scanning per-entry tibble construction linear character-vector scanning single-pass column assembly. Parsing ~7,000 entries dropped ~100 s ~17 s R 4.5.2 / Windows.

title: scimapR 0.1.0
text: scimapR comprehensive R toolkit bibliometric scientometric analysis: reproducible, equity-aware, question-driven, AI-assisted toolkit working biomedical researchers. Designed complement foundational bibliometrix package (Aria & Cuccurullo, 2017) first-class round-trip interop.

title: scimapR 0.1.0

Reproducible--construction corpus certificates. sm_certificate(), sm_rebuild_from_cert(), sm_verify_certificate(). Author trajectory analysis. sm_author_trajectory() topic pivots, collaborator turnover, emerging-collaborator detection. Equity representation audit. sm_audit_geographic(), sm_audit_gender(), sm_audit_funding(), sm_audit_oa() built-confidence reporting limitation caveats. LLM-grounded corpus chat. sm_chat() retrieval-constrained citations.
